title: ICC ODI World Cup 2027: India opens against Australia, faces Pakistan on October 10
excerpt: The 14th edition runs October 2 to November 21, 2027 across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, with 57 matches in 12 venues and a revamped Super Sevens format.
body:
• The ICC unveiled the fixtures for the 14th ICC Men's ODI World Cup, to be played from October 2 to November 21, 2027, across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia — 57 matches at 12 venues.
  • India opens its campaign on October 7, 2027 against defending champions Australia at Newlands, Cape Town — a rematch of the 2023 final — before facing Pakistan in Johannesburg on October 10.
  • The tournament has a revamped format: a three-team Super Series (Oct 2–6), a 12-team group stage, then a Super Sevens round before the semi-finals on November 17–18 and the final on November 21 in Johannesburg.
  • What it means for you: all matches are listed in IST. India's 1:30 pm IST starts translate to 4:00 am ET / 1:00 am PT in the US, so set the DVR. The ICC opened a ticket ballot alongside the schedule — fans planning travel to South Africa should register early.

India's road to the 2027 ODI World Cup will begin with the sternest possible test. The ICC on October 1 unveiled the fixtures for the 14th edition of the tournament, which runs from October 2 to November 21, 2027 across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia — and India will open its campaign on October 7 against Australia at Newlands in Cape Town, a rematch of the 2023 final.

Three days later, on October 10, comes the fixture the cricketing world always circles: India versus Pakistan at the Wanderers in Johannesburg. The 57-match tournament will be played across 12 venues over seven weeks.

Context & Background

This is the first ODI World Cup to be held in Africa since 2003, and the first to be co-hosted by three nations — South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. Australia arrive as defending champions after beating India by six wickets in the 2023 final at Ahmedabad, a defeat that lends extra edge to the 2027 opener.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=wLmCT03mp3c

India's Group A draw is a heavyweight one: alongside Australia and Pakistan are Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and a Qualifier A side. Group B comprises New Zealand, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, England and Qualifier B. The qualifiers are still to be decided via a three-team Super Series in Windhoek from October 2 to 6, between the 12th- to 14th-ranked teams.

India's Fixtures

India's five group-stage matches, all starting at 1:30 pm IST:

  • October 7: India vs Australia, Newlands, Cape Town
  • October 10: India vs Pakistan, Wanderers, Johannesburg
  • October 14: India vs Afghanistan, SuperSport Park, Tshwane
  • October 17: India vs Qualifier A, Mangaung Oval, Bloemfontein
  • October 24: Zimbabwe vs India, Victoria Falls (Zimbabwe)

The India–Zimbabwe game at Victoria Falls will be the first World Cup fixture at the new Mosi-oa-Tunya Stadium, according to tournament coverage.

Impact & Analysis

The revamped format is the story beyond the fixtures. The top three teams from each group, plus the better fourth-placed side across both groups, advance to the Super Sevens — a seven-team second round from October 25 to November 14, with no points carried forward and each team playing six round-robin matches before the top four reach the semi-finals.

Teams are pre-seeded into Super Sevens positions — India is A1, Australia A2, Pakistan A3, New Zealand B1, South Africa B2, Sri Lanka B3, and England takes the fourth-placed slot. The format rewards sustained performance across two rounds rather than a single group-stage sprint, reducing the jeopardy of one bad week.

For India, the early schedule is unforgiving: Australia and Pakistan first up means the campaign's tone will be set within four days. But it also means the two biggest fixtures are done before the Super Sevens, where the real attrition begins.

Diaspora Angle

South Africa has one of the oldest Indian diasporas in the world, and venues like Durban and Johannesburg are expected to draw large Indian-origin crowds. For fans in the United States, the timing is brutal but manageable: India's 1:30 pm IST starts land at 4:00 am ET (1:00 am PT), so plan accordingly. The ICC opened a ticket ballot along with the schedule — anyone considering travel should register interest now rather than wait.

What's Next

The semi-finals are scheduled for November 17 in Cape Town and November 18 in Tshwane (Centurion), with the final on November 21 at the Wanderers in Johannesburg. The remaining qualifier spots and team seedings will be confirmed through the qualification pathway over the next year, and squad announcements will follow closer to the tournament. India will be looking to end a wait that stretches back to 2011 for an ODI World Cup title — and the road starts against the team that broke their hearts in Ahmedabad.
